add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: After the rename to ScreenedEmail (86647f0a54, 2013-08-14) should_block? still did an exact ScreenedEmail.where(email: email) lookup. Commit 'Emails are case insensitive' (01a68f8cc7, 2014-07-16) added before_save :downcase_email to ScreenedEmail, before_validation :downcase_email to User, and compares se.email.downcase with email.downcase in should_block?. Today's screened_email.rb still downcases on save and canonical() downcases the input, so casing no longer bypasses a block.

On main today ScreenedEmail.should_block? still calls screened_email.record_match! on a match, and ScreeningModel#record_match! (lib/screening_model.rb) still does self.match_count += 1, sets last_match_at and calls save: a non-atomic read-modify-write run from EmailValidator during validation. The history of screened_email.rb and screening_model.rb after the merge shows no change to this side effect (only refactors, the levenshtein lookup and annotations).

The unanchored Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) stayed (later "@(.+\\.)?(#{domains})" in PR #3463 and 69ad0358c2, 2015) with no end anchor, so gmail.com.evil.com matched. Commit 'SECURITY: email domain whitelist could be bypassed' (2a22b90538, 2018-01-17) appended $ to the regex, with a spec for email.computers.are.evil.com; today's EmailValidator.email_in_restriction_setting? still uses "@(.+\\.)?(#{domains})$". Subdomain matching (evil.example.com for example.com) is intended behaviour upstream since 2015; the suffix bypass is what was fixed.
